newsitem.title: UK: FTSE 100 opens up in muted response to NY's surge.
newsitem.headline: FTSE 100 opens up in muted response to NY's surge.

text.p: The FTSE 100 opened higher after the Dow ended 153.8 points up at 7,758.06, having stood about 46 points higher at London market close.
The UK index was 31.4 points up at 4,627.7 by 0738 GMT.
Potential gains on the back of the U.S. surge were limited by continuing nervousness over Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown's first Budget on July 2 and worries over interest rates.
A test of sentiment will come at this morning's auction of two billion stg 10-year gilts with the result due at 1015 GMT. Cover is seen at least two times with some dealers expecting three times.

"Wall Street will give a reasonable tone to the market this morning and the gilts auction will be a test of sentiment but until we get rid of the clouds surrounding Gordon Brown's maiden budget we'll not make any great progress," said NatWest strategist David McBain.
